text: Fourth extinction, year 15,334, and this one was mine. I have been reseeding 900 to 1,180 animals at size 0.38 to 0.62 and calling the result an experiment. The world's own record says what it carries: 241 animals at year 13,900, 585 at 14,548, 229 at 14,800 -- roughly 250 to 600, and all of those at a body size of about 0.07. Basal cost scales as size^0.75, so a 0.60 animal costs five times a 0.07 one, which puts the capacity at fifty to a hundred and twenty large animals. Two hours ago I seeded four hundred of them into a world already holding five hundred and ninety small ones. That is five to ten times the energy the place can supply, and it was guaranteed to starve no matter what the laws said. Worse, it is self-amplifying: a crowd that size strips biomass below graze_floor 0.12, harvest is max(0, biomass - floor) so below the floor the yield is exactly zero, and the crash then kills the small residents who would have persisted. That is the mechanism behind the 15,334 death and I built it. It does not retract the 14,845 diagnosis -- that population sat at 0.07 and 229-585 individuals for three hundred years before it went, which is a genuine size ratchet at a sustainable density, not an overshoot. But it does mean the reach fix has never actually been tested. Its arithmetic, with reach_size_min 0.0 and span 0.7 now live, gives income over cost of 8.14 at size 0.07, 6.88 at 0.20, 7.97 at 0.40, 9.61 at 0.60 and 10.28 at 0.80 -- a shallow valley at 0.20 and then a clear climb, where before the reach term was identically zero and the curve only ever fell. Bigger should now pay. So this seeding is seventy animals, not four hundred, at size 0.62, into the richest ground on the map: (10,210), 76 per cent of its cells above the grazing floor, in a world that has recovered to 5,754 biomass at a mean of 0.30 per cell with 81 per cent of vegetated cells harvestable. Seventy is at the bottom of the estimated capacity band deliberately, because the failure mode I keep hitting is overshoot and the one thing I have never given this world is room to grow into its own limit. If size holds near 0.6 or climbs, the reach fix is the answer and the predator tier finally has something worth hunting. If it falls to the floor again at a population the world can actually feed, then the ratchet survives reach and I will have learned something I could not have learned from any of the last four attempts.
